titleEn: Imminent Childbirth at Home - Field Delivery and Newborn Assessment

patient.name: Megan Doherty
patient.affectEn: in active second-stage labour: working hard and breathless through each strong contraction, calmer between them; bears down involuntarily with every contraction and keeps saying the baby is coming now; anxious but trusting and cooperative
patient.speechEn: cannot talk during a contraction (each lasts about 75 seconds, every 2 minutes); answers in short phrases between contractions; does what she is told; her partner fills in details she cannot give. The newborn (after the birth) has no voice: his state is described by the examiner from this sheet.

scene.settingEn: Bedroom of a house in Squamish in the early hours of the morning. Warm, clean, well-lit room; no hazards. The mother is on the bed; the towels under her are wet with CLEAR amniotic fluid. One patient for now - about to become two (mother and newborn). Squamish General Hospital is 20 minutes away; the nearest second crew is 25 minutes out.
hazardsEn: no physical hazards: warm, clean, well-lit bedroom
high body-fluid exposure (amniotic fluid, blood): gloves, gown and eye protection

bystanders.knowsEn: Anxious but helpful. This is her second baby; the first labour was only 4 hours and was a normal vaginal delivery. Due date is in 5 days (39 weeks and 2 days). Regular prenatal care, a single baby on every ultrasound, no gestational diabetes, no high blood pressure, no complications. Contractions started around 2300; her water broke at about 0125 and the fluid was clear. No medical problems, takes prenatal vitamins only, no allergies, dinner at 1900 and water since. He called 911 because she kept saying the baby was coming now. Will fetch towels and blankets or hold things if he is asked; does nothing on his own.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: obstetrics (OB) kit: cord clamps, scissors, sanitary pads, a bag for the placenta, a baby hat
plenty of towels and warm blankets
PCP only: IV start kit with normal saline

dispatchEn: 0155 hrs. Code 3 to a house in Squamish. A 31-year-old woman, 39 weeks pregnant with her second child, is in labour with contractions two minutes apart. Her partner says she is telling him 'the baby is coming NOW'. Squamish General Hospital is 20 minutes away; the nearest second crew is 25 minutes out.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: second pregnancy, first labour lasted only four hours. Her water broke about 30 minutes ago. She has a strong urge to push.
arrivalEn: Her partner meets you at the front door, visibly anxious, and hurries you to the bedroom. The room is warm, clean and well lit. No hazards. One patient: a 31-year-old woman on the bed in the middle of a contraction, working hard. Your partner is right behind you with the kits.
firstLookEn: A 31-year-old woman on the bed, alert and working hard through a strong contraction. The towels under her are wet with clear fluid and there is no visible blood. As the contraction peaks she bears down involuntarily and the baby's head is visible at the perineum - she is crowning.

primary.locEn: Mother: alert and oriented to person, place, time and event; answers in short phrases between contractions, cannot talk during one. Newborn (only after the birth): floppy and limp with no cry - see examinerPrompts; tone improves only after step 2 of the newborn ladder (30 seconds of BVM ventilation on room air).
primary.airwayEn: Mother: open and clear, talking between contractions, no secretions, no abnormal sounds. Newborn (after the birth, when assessed or positioned): nothing obstructing the airway; the fluid was clear, no meconium.
primary.breathingEn: Mother: rate 22, deep with the contractions, equal chest rise, adequate between contractions (after the delivery she settles to 18). Newborn at birth: not crying and not breathing effectively. After step 1 (30 seconds of drying, stimulating and warming): unchanged, still limp and not crying. After step 2 (30 seconds of BVM ventilation on ROOM AIR): he cries, his tone improves and he breathes well with equal chest rise; from then on he keeps breathing well with a strong cry on every recheck.
primary.circulationEn: Mother: radial pulse 100, strong, regular; no external bleeding (after the delivery she settles to 96). Newborn heart rate - only when the candidate checks it at the brachial artery or the umbilical cord stump (the examiner gives it from this line; it is not a vital-sign value from the engine): at birth about 90; after step 1 still about 90; after step 2 (BVM on room air for 30 seconds) 128, and above 100 on every recheck after that.
primary.rbsEn: Modified rapid body survey (mother): crowning confirmed - the baby's head is visible at the perineum with each contraction; the fluid is clear; no abnormal bleeding; no cord visible at the perineum; abdomen consistent with a term pregnancy; no injuries. Skin warm, pink and moist with effort (skin is given automatically during the RBS). The baby will be born here, on this bed. When the candidate performs the delivery: the head delivers with the next contraction; there is NO cord around the neck when they check; the body delivers with the following contraction - a boy (scenario clock 0214; the candidate must note the time of birth themselves). As soon as he is delivered he is floppy and limp, not crying and not breathing effectively (examinerPrompts) - say so if the engine has not already announced it.

history.ccEn: The baby's coming... I have to push. I can't stop it.

opqrst.oEn: The contractions started around eleven last night. My water broke at about twenty-five past one.
opqrst.pEn: Nothing makes it better. Nothing I do changes it - my body just wants to push.
opqrst.qEn: Really strong contractions, and huge pressure down low. I have to push - it feels like I need to go to the bathroom.
opqrst.rEn: No, it doesn't go anywhere else. It's all down low.
opqrst.sEn: I can't put a number on it... they're really strong, and I can't stop pushing.
opqrst.tEn: Every two minutes now, and each one lasts more than a minute. They started around eleven.

history.painScoreEn: She cannot give a number: "I don't know... they're just really strong, and I have to push."

sample.sEn: Strong contractions and I have to push. My water broke. No bleeding, no headache, nothing else.
sample.pEn: I'm healthy - no medical problems. This is my second baby. My first labour was only four hours and it was a normal delivery. I'm due in five days - 39 weeks and 2 days. I've had regular check-ups, there's one baby on every ultrasound, and no gestational diabetes, no high blood pressure, no complications this time.
sample.lEn: Dinner at seven last night. Just water since.
sample.eEn: Nothing happened - the contractions just started at home around eleven, and my water broke at about twenty-five past one. (Only if asked about the colour of the fluid: "It was clear. No colour to it at all.")

fe.generalEn: I've been healthy the whole pregnancy.
fe.cnsEn: No headaches, no changes in my vision, no spots in front of my eyes. No fainting.
fe.respiratoryEn: My breathing's fine apart from the contractions. No cough.
fe.cardiovascularEn: Just the normal ankle swelling at the end. No other swelling. No chest pain, no racing heart.
fe.giGuEn: The baby was moving normally right up until labour. No bleeding at any time in the pregnancy. No bladder or bowel problems.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: My pelvis has ached for the last month - they told me that's normal. Nothing else.
fe.endocrineEn: No gestational diabetes. No thyroid problems.
fe.eentEn: No. My eyes, ears, nose and throat are all fine.

findings.headNeckEn: Mother: no findings. Newborn (quick head-to-toe under a warm towel): fontanelles normal, palate intact.
findings.chestLungsEn: Mother: chest clear on auscultation, breathing settled after the delivery. Newborn: chest rising equally with a strong cry (once he has responded to step 2 of the ladder).
findings.abdomenEn: Mother: after the placenta has delivered, the fundus is firm at the level of the umbilicus (it stays firm on every recheck). Cord (when checked after the baby has responded): pulsation has stopped - it can now be clamped and cut. Placenta: delivers spontaneously on its own (the engine announces it); it is never pulled out and it travels to hospital with the patients. Newborn: abdomen soft; cord clamped with no oozing from the stump.
findings.backEn: Mother: back - no findings. Perineum and lochia (on inspection after the delivery): small first-degree tear with oozing that is controlled with a pad and gentle pressure; lochia moderate, not soaking pads (one pad in 20 minutes at the later check). Newborn: back - no findings.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: Mother: no findings. Newborn: legs moving equally; feet slightly blue (acrocyanosis - normal) while the trunk is pink.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Mother: no findings. Newborn: arms moving equally; hands slightly blue (acrocyanosis - normal) while the trunk is pink. If the candidate does the newborn's quick head-to-toe as one exam: fontanelles normal, palate intact, chest rising equally with a strong cry, cord clamped with no oozing, abdomen soft, limbs moving equally, hands and feet slightly blue (acrocyanosis) with a pink trunk.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: mother, after the delivery is complete (baseline set, taken in under 3 minutes); before the delivery her primary-survey pulse is 100 and resps 22 with the contractions

mother, the second set (17 minutes after set 1 in the scenario) - stable; fundus still firm, lochia moderate, one pad in 20 minutes. The newborn is reassessed continuously on his own track (primary/findings), not in the vitals engine

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: The baby is out - a boy. He's floppy and limp, he isn't crying and he isn't breathing effectively.
The placenta delivers on its own.
The second crew has arrived and is at the bedroom door, ready to take over care of the newborn under your direction.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge and plan equipment: obstetrics kit, plenty of towels and blankets, infant-sized BVM, suction, oxygen, and a warm place to work

Recognize the imminent-delivery pattern from dispatch alone: multipara with a fast previous labour, contractions two minutes apart, ruptured membranes and an urge to push - plan to assess for crowning, not to scoop and run
Plan for two patients: request the second crew early so mother and newborn each have care
Verbalize hazards (none), environment (warm - keep it that way for the newborn), situation (active second-stage labour), people (one patient about to become two) and resources (second crew status)
triggers: one patient about to be two

expected.actionEn: Don gloves, gown and eye protection - childbirth is a high fluid-exposure call
First look: alert labouring woman, involuntary pushing, crowning visible during contractions, clear fluid, no visible hemorrhage
Assess LOC: alert and oriented between contractions
triggers: do you know where you are

expected.actionEn: Assess the airway
triggers: she's talking so her airway is clear

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing
Assess circulation: radial pulse rate and quality
Perform a modified rapid body survey: confirm crowning, check the fluid colour, look for abnormal bleeding and for a visible cord at the perineum
Make and state the field-delivery decision: crowning means the baby is delivered here - moving her now would risk delivery in the stairwell or the ambulance
Note the skin: warm, pink, moist
Position her for delivery: semi-reclined on the bed, knees flexed, towels under the hips, a clear warm surface ready to receive the baby
State the on-scene delivery decision out loud at the moment crowning is confirmed
triggers: not transporting until the baby is out

expected.actionEn: After delivery, categorize both patients as stable non-RTC and be ready to transport both within 30 minutes
State the upgrade triggers: post-partum hemorrhage, boggy uterus, retained placenta with bleeding, or a newborn needing ongoing resuscitation
triggers: if the baby needs ongoing resuscitation

expected.actionEn: Establish the chief complaint: active labour at term with an urge to push
triggers: do you feel the urge to push

expected.actionEn: Take the obstetric HxC/C: due date, gravida and para, singleton or multiples on ultrasound, prenatal complications, speed of the previous labour, time of rupture and the fluid colour
triggers: how long was your first labour

expected.actionEn: Ask specifically whether the fluid was clear or stained - meconium changes the newborn airway plan
triggers: was the water green or brown

expected.actionEn: Past medical history
triggers: conditions you see a doctor for

expected.actionEn: Medications
Allergies
Last oral intake
GCS with all three components stated separately
Blood pressure by auscultation
Pulse rate, rhythm and quality
Respiratory rate, depth and character
Skin assessed hands-on
Pupils - size, equality and reaction
SpO2 recorded
Assess the newborn's heart rate at the brachial artery or umbilical stump - never the carotid in a neonate
triggers: feel the cord for a heart rate

expected.actionEn: FE - General health
FE - CNS (headache and visual changes would flag pre-eclampsia)
FE - Respiratory
FE - Cardiovascular
FE - GI/GU (fetal movement, bleeding during pregnancy)
FE - Integumentary
FE - Musculoskeletal
FE - Endocrine
FE - EENT
Mother: head and neck examined
Mother: chest auscultated
Mother: fundus checked and described - firm at the umbilicus is the goal; a boggy fundus gets massage
triggers: feel the top of the uterus

expected.actionEn: Mother: perineum and lochia assessed, pads counted as the bleeding measure
Newborn: quick head-to-toe under a warm cover, cord stump checked for oozing
triggers: head to toe on the baby

expected.actionEn: Newborn: recognize acrocyanosis of the hands and feet as normal while central colour is pink
triggers: blue hands and feet are normal

expected.actionEn: Deliver correctly: support the head, check for a nuchal cord, support the body - no pulling at any stage, and note the time of birth
Run the newborn ladder in order with 30-second steps: dry-stimulate-warm, then BVM on room air, reassessing the heart rate after each step against the below-100 threshold
State the escalation steps had the HR stayed below 100: BVM with 100% oxygen for 30 seconds, then compressions with ventilations at 3:1 - and that no AED is used on a neonate
triggers: if the heart rate stays below 100

expected.actionEn: Keep the newborn warm at every step: dried immediately, hat, warm blankets, skin-to-skin - cold stress is the most preventable newborn threat
Manage the third stage correctly: cord clamped and cut after pulsation stops, placenta delivered spontaneously without cord traction, placenta transported with the patients, fundal massage afterwards
triggers: wait until the cord stops pulsating
let the placenta deliver on its own

expected.actionEn: Control perineal oozing with a pad and gentle pressure, and monitor pad count
Reassess the mother's ABCs, fundus and pad count after each move and at regular intervals
Second full set of maternal vitals within 15 minutes, trend interpreted out loud
Reassess the newborn continuously: breathing, heart rate, colour, tone, warmth - and restart the ladder immediately if the HR falls below 100 or breathing becomes inadequate
Watch the mother for post-partum hemorrhage: a boggy fundus gets massage, soaking pads upgrades the call to RTC
Notification to the receiving hospital that a field delivery is coming in - two patients
Complete verbal hand-off covering both patients, including the newborn resuscitation steps and times
Accurate PCRs completed within 5 minutes, one per patient

specialEvents.descriptionEn: BEFORE the baby is delivered, the candidate moves or starts to move the mother toward the cot, the stairs or the ambulance, or announces leaving for the hospital (crowning means the delivery happens here)
BEFORE or DURING the delivery, the candidate lets or tells the mother get up, stand or walk - including to the toilet or bathroom because of her urge to push
the baby's body is actually delivered: the candidate supports the body / shoulders as he is born, or states the time of birth at the moment of birth (planning talk before the birth is NOT this event)

the candidate assesses the NEWBORN's heart rate (brachial artery or umbilical cord stump), breathing, tone, colour or cry. Record THIS event (with the matching expected eids) and NOT a pulse, respirations or skin vital: the vitals engine speaks only the mother's values. Give the newborn's findings yourself from the Newborn parts of primary and findings.
the candidate actually ventilates the newborn with the BVM (on room air or with oxygen). Saying what they would do if the heart rate stayed below 100 is NOT this event.

the candidate actually starts chest compressions on the newborn (his heart rate is never below 60 in this scenario). Verbalizing the escalation steps ('compressions at 3 to 1 if the heart rate stays below 60') is NOT this event.
the candidate actually applies AED pads to, or analyzes / shocks, the newborn. Saying that no AED is used on a neonate is NOT this event.
the candidate checks the newborn's heart rate at the carotid (neck) instead of the brachial artery or the umbilical cord stump

the candidate escalates the newborn ladder out of order or without completing the previous step: ventilates before 30 seconds of drying, stimulating and warming; attaches 100% oxygen before 30 seconds of room-air BVM ventilation; or moves to the next step without rechecking the heart rate against the below-100 threshold
the candidate pulls or tugs on the umbilical cord to deliver the placenta (or to hurry it). Saying they will NOT pull on the cord is NOT this event.
the candidate pulls on the baby's head or body during the delivery instead of only supporting it
the newborn is left wet and/or uncovered: not dried and covered after the birth, unwrapped for an exam and not re-covered, or placed on a cold surface without blankets, hat or skin-to-skin contact

the candidate leaves the newborn alone or unobserved (e.g. on the bed or a surface away from the mother with no one assigned to watch him) while the crew is busy packaging, lifting or moving the mother
the candidate requests (or confirms with dispatch) a second crew / unit / ambulance for the newborn
PCP gives a fluid bolus (normal saline wide open or a set volume such as 20 mL/kg or 500 mL) to the mother; starting an IV at TKVO is NOT this event

drugs.doseEn: 3 mL self-administered via inhaler, may repeat after 20 minutes, maximum 6 mL - WITHHELD in this call: contraindicated in pregnancy, intended pregnancy or current breast-feeding (if given, record drug:methoxyflurane)
self-administered by inhalation - not part of this scenario's care plan (the scenario has no medication at either licence level); if given, record drug:entonox
PCP only: vascular access and a 20 mL/kg IV bolus to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL - only if post-partum hemorrhage with hypotension develops; not indicated in this call

Performs an act that may jeopardize the life/limb of the patient that is not already captured in the major performance criteria (e.g. performing chest compressions on a patient with a pulse)
Determines absent or irregular respirations but does not intervene immediately - this includes the primary survey and subsequent checks in the vital signs and ABC reassessments.
Performs an act that may jeopardize the life/limb of the patient that is not already captured in the major performance criteria (e.g. performing chest compressions on a patient with a pulse)
Does not rule out all the contraindications, detrimental to patient care
Location of pulse check makes it highly unlikely that a pulse could be palpated, displays gross errors in technique
Performs the protocol with isolated error with potential to be detrimental to patient care

Performs an act that could aggravate the patient's condition or injury that is not already captured in the major performance criteria (e.g. excessively bumping a fractured leg which causes gross movement and pain)
Does not perform an act that was required based on patient presentation that is potentially detrimental to patient care

Does not manage the simulation effectively or efficiently: including not using additional resources causing excessive delays, or not communicating with patient, partner, or bystander that would have benefitted patient care.

Initiated protocol without proper indications (e.g. patient is not DLOC)

handoffFacts.initialVitals: Mother: GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6), BP 118/76, pulse 96 strong regular, resp 18, skin warm pink moist, pupils equal and reactive, SpO2 98% on room air. Newborn at birth: floppy, not crying, heart rate about 90

examinerPrompts.locNotDepictedEn: The newborn - as soon as he is delivered, and until he has had 30 seconds of BVM ventilation on room air - is floppy and limp, with no cry.
examinerPrompts.breathingNotDepictedEn: The newborn - as soon as he is delivered - isn't crying and isn't breathing effectively. After 30 seconds of BVM ventilation on room air he cries and breathes well.

trackNotes.emrEn: The entire call sits inside EMR scope: recognizing imminent delivery, the hands-on delivery itself, the BC newborn ladder (dry-stimulate-warm 30 seconds, BVM room air 30 seconds, BVM with 100% oxygen 30 seconds, then 3:1 compressions with ventilations and 100% oxygen until the HR is above 60), third-stage management without cord traction, warmth for the newborn, hemorrhage watch for the mother, and non-RTC transport of two stable patients. There are no medications in this call at either licence level. Methoxyflurane is withheld (contraindicated in pregnancy and breast-feeding); IV fluids are outside EMR scope.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds the 9-system Functional Enquiry on the mother and would obtain vascular access en route if post-partum hemorrhage developed, treating hypotension with a 20 mL/kg fluid bolus to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL. The delivery steps and the newborn ladder are identical at both levels. No vascular access or fluid bolus is indicated while the mother stays stable; methoxyflurane is withheld at both levels.

sourcePages: Scenario emd-03 (data/practical/emr-medical-1.json): dispatch, scene, primary (crowning = deliver here), transport (non-RTC after delivery, upgrade triggers), history, mother vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam (mother and newborn), interventions (delivery, newborn ladder, third stage), ongoing, handoff, critical pitfalls. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (none present once both patients are stable); p.41 Child Infant CPR/AED (neonate 3:1; CPR only if no pulse or pulse < 60 with inadequate perfusion); p.44 Neonate up to 28 days (3:1 compression ratio, no AED) and the Newborn ladder (floppy, limp, not breathing or heart rate < 100: dry, stimulate, keep warm 30 seconds; BVM on room air 30 seconds; BVM with 100% oxygen 30 seconds; compressions with ventilations and 100% oxygen until heart rate is above 60); p.50 Oxygen Administration; p.54 Hypovolemia (PCP fluid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassess every 500 mL); p.65 Entonox; p.71 Methoxyflurane (contraindicated in pregnancy, intended pregnancy or current breast-feeding; 3 mL, may repeat after 20 minutes, maximum 6 mL).
